source.title: Epistemological Case Studies
allPromptTexts: Provide a list of 20 epistemological case studies for students of rationality.
How might these scenarios best be taught in a 60-minute class of 10 students?
Explain the value of epistemological case studies or scenarios.
Create a 10-item quiz on the entire thread above.
Provide 15 discussion questions relevant to the content above.
source.preamble: All four highlight extracts read; four clearly labeled edited highlights. Original contents list replaced with exact prompt navigation.

responseDecisions.1.1: Preserved all twenty titles/order; corrected court provenance, finite distinct books, quantum metaphors, random-selection conflation, sensory-concept inference and predictive-policing inference. Made polygraph rates expressly hypothetical and testable; other sound scenarios retained.
responseDecisions.1.2: Preserved twenty paragraph cases/order. Qualified investment records, placebo causality, cultural relativism, skepticism and historical legends; corrected Jung and bodhisattva descriptions, distinguished reliability from ethics and search assumptions.
responseDecisions.1.3: Preserved twenty entries/order; corrected Gettier, error types, Sleeping Beauty and Bostrom; separated circumstantial evidence, model assumptions, observer selection and causal inference. Retained remaining open investigations.
responseDecisions.2.1: Retained preparation, three fifteen-minute rounds, reflection and homework hierarchy. Filled missing five minutes via ten-minute reflection; explicit group participation and minute allocations.
responseDecisions.2.2: Retained 10/40/10 structure and nested questions. Two cases/five pairs; filled previously unspecified exploration time with comparison and individual revision. Replaced leading questions with open questions.
responseDecisions.2.3: Retained 5/25/20/10 structure and two groups of five. Corrected infeasible twenty-case promise to four selected cases, explicit roles and reports. Other cases remain homework menu.
responseDecisions.3.1: Seven value headings preserved; replaced guarantees with teaching aims and made assessment, revision, perspective-taking and transfer concrete.
responseDecisions.3.2: Seven benefits preserved; corrected unsupported memory superiority and added ways to check learning; retained effective discussion of application and reasoning.
responseDecisions.3.3: Six philosophical uses retained. Distinguished imagined counterexamples from empirical evidence and defeasible intuitions from settled verdicts.
responseDecisions.4.1: Ten questions/keys retained; disambiguated three tracks, updated schedule and revision criteria; manually checked all answers.
responseDecisions.4.2: Ten questions/keys retained; corrected placebo cause inference and its answer; other questions remain aligned.
responseDecisions.4.3: Ten questions/keys retained; replaced unrelated suffix-sphere question with Sleeping Beauty; synchronized four-case lesson answer.
responseDecisions.5.1: Fifteen questions retained; corrected infinity, quantum, random-selection and policing assumptions; eleven retained verbatim.
responseDecisions.5.2: Fifteen questions retained; corrected scenario numbers 6→8 and 11→13, placebo/bodhisattva assumptions, and case-superiority presupposition; ten retained verbatim.
responseDecisions.5.3: All fifteen questions retained: they remain open, relevant to their actual cases, and invite critique of the teaching plan.

research.use: Primary ancient account directly read; an attributed story, not a verified court record.
Jung text directly read: inherited archetypal forms; hypothesis distinguished from shared learned facts.
Original paper read, especially first job/coins case; justified true belief with epistemic luck.
Original Elga article/setup read: fair coin, Monday/Tuesday, memory erasure; no random waking intervals.
Original Bostrom article abstract and argument read: conditional disjunction, not an unconditional simulation claim.
Official handbook: Type I/II definitions relative to null hypothesis.
Indexed primary review abstract: randomized placebo versus no-treatment comparison. Direct PubMed response was inconsistent; no full-text claim.
Publisher/translator indexed glossary directly supports aspiration to buddhahood to benefit beings; direct open returned 502. Used only bounded glossary claim, not full sutra.
Indexed research abstract on three-arm comparisons; confirms why within-group improvement does not isolate treatment causality.

remainingConcerns: The lesson plans are worked editorial proposals, not empirically tested curricula or claims of guaranteed learning.
Polygraph figures are expressly invented for arithmetic; no real accuracy estimate is claimed.

Some cases are conceptual puzzles with disputed answers. Historical story and religious interpretations are qualified; 84000 direct retrieval failed but its indexed glossary supports the limited correction.
